note: No rule of the Monetary Authority of Macao fixing an account number's length was read. Two banks' own lengths were: the Government Information Bureau's release of 9 April 2018 (read 2026-10-30) reports the Social Security Fund's confirmation from the Bank of China Macau Branch that its account numbers rose from 12 to 15 digits with a system upgrade, online banking showing 17 because the first two digits are 00, and that old and new numbers can both be used; HSBC Macau's customer information sheet for inward payments (May 2025, read 2026-10-30) says its account number must be 12 digits, the first three the branch code. So the number is written as 12 to 15 digits, and a new account is drawn at fifteen, the Bank of China's (which bank is the largest wasn't read). A payee's number at another bank of another length, or the Bank of China's written with its two leading zeros, would be refused; no other bank's length was read. The receiving bank is named beside the number, not in it, and no check digit is published.

sources.title: Government Information Bureau of the Macao SAR, Bank's System Upgrade does not Affect the Services of the FSS (9 April 2018)
sources.said: Social Security Fund 2018-04-09 ... After confirming with the Bank of China Macau Branch, the FSS was told that the bank account numbers had increased from 12 to 15 digits after the bank system upgrade (the online banking shows 17 digits because the first two digits are 00). However, the middle part of the new account number is still the same as the old one. Both old and new account numbers can be used.

sources.title: HSBC Macau, Customer information sheet for inward payments to Macau (May 2025)
sources.said: Account number of HSBC Macau must be 12 digits. Branch code is the first 3 digits and the following 9 digits are account number.
